items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-05-10
items.q: Freddie Kepard, Big Eye Louie, Eddie Vincent, Jimmy Fall Out.

ctx.x: Have a banjo player, a guitar player? Let's see, they used violin.

Yeah, the guitar player with them, but I don't know how kind of a drummer. Drama? Let's see. No, Freddie Kepard with them. Freddie Kepard, Big Eye Louie, Eddie Vincent, Jimmy Fall Out. Bro, he must have been some right there, a drummer.
I'm not sure, but I think maybe Dink Johnson played with them a while. Do you ever know him?

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1959-12-09
items.q: And Eddie Vinson played a vowel trombone you know. And he drilled me through what we were going to play.

ctx.x: Right across the street is the little double house back in the yard. That's where Eddie used to live. Eddie Vinson and Tom Alvin on one side. Oh I see. And I used to go down there and join them every day. They had the bass violin player they called Teep. And when I first come down there I could play the bass. I was a little bit of a fellow. But Tom wanted the cornet playing. He said, get your cornet. We'll all show you. And Eddie Vinson played a vowel trombone you know. And he drilled me through what we were…

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-01-16
items.q: And Eddie Vincent was practicing every day with us.

ctx.x: Would it be 1900 or would it be 1910 or 1920 or what?

No, I don't think it was that far back. That's it. Dewey used to wait on Basin Street, Emmanuel Perez. That's when I was very small. Yeah, that must bring back. Let's see, wait, I got to get that thing straight. I think Tom could tell you better than I could about that. Tom Alba? Yeah. Because I had learned how to play cornet, you know, and Tom was playing the violin. And Eddie Vincent was practicing every day with us. And then all at once he picked up and he left there with Jimmy Fallon and then we went north.…
